raised.claim: The created issue body puts model-authored prose ahead of the rendered ```triage-scope block, and parseScopeBlock takes the FIRST fence match, so a fence inside the model's body wins.
raised.why_it_breaks: buildTriagePrompt feeds the model the bodies of the open issues (`${i.body.slice(0, ISSUE_BODY_CAP)}`), which after this change contain our ```triage-scope fences, so a new_issue body that echoes that format (or contains any fenced example) ends up BEFORE the block we append. On the next run BLOCK_RE.exec(`/```triage-scope\s*\n([\s\S]*?)\n?```/`) returns the model's earlier match: if it happens to be valid JSON, guard 2 evaluates every future row against a scope that guard 1 never inspected (guard 1 only sees the structured field), silently accepting or refusing rows on a scope nobody wrote; if it is not valid JSON, parseScopeBlock returns null, the issue is unscoped and refuses every future row. This is the same silent-wrong-scope class this PR fixed for `contains` values, left open on the body path — the render comment's claim that "the model never authors the text" does not hold, because the model authors `issue.body`, which is part of the parsed input.

raised.claim: Verdicts that guard 3 degrades from not_on_untappd to matcher_bug are counted as `wontfix` in the persisted outcome and the digest line.
raised.why_it_breaks: Guard 3 pushes `{...verdict, review_class: 'matcher_bug'}` into plan.quiet, and the quiet loop increments `outcome.wontfix` for every quiet verdict that is not not_on_untappd. A run with no search dep that degrades, say, 6 unproven absence verdicts writes 6 `matcher_bug` rows to enrich_failures (kept in the enrichment pool) but publishes `Тріаж: ... 6 wontfix` through buildTriageLine, so an operator reading the digest concludes those rows were declared permanently unfixable when the opposite (retry under BACKOFF_HOURS) is what the DB says.

raised.claim: Guard 2 (row vs scope) is only applied to verdicts routed to an existing issue; verdicts that create a NEW issue are never checked against the scope they propose.
raised.why_it_breaks: The model proposes new_issue k1 with scope `{beer_ids: [], where: [{col:'candidates_count', op:'>', value: 0}]}` and attaches beer 1 whose row has candidates_count = 0. The else branch checks only `allowedKeys`, so the plan creates the issue and comments beer 1 into it: `renderScopeBlock` then stamps the body with `candidates_count > 0` while the issue's own founding example has 0, and from the next run every zero-candidate row of that same pattern is refused by guard 2. rowSatisfiesScope is called nowhere on this path, so the one invariant this PR enforces (no consequence without evidence from the row) is not checked for the rows that found a new issue.

raised.claim: The strict-tool-use mirror declares `value` as string|number|null for every col/op, while ScopeTermSchema requires a number for numeric columns and no value at all for empty/non_empty/is_null/is_not_null, so a schema-permitted payload can fail the zod union and reject the whole analysis.
raised.why_it_breaks: Nothing in ANALYSIS_TOOL_SCHEMA tells the model which type `value` must have per column, so it can legally emit `{col:'candidates_count', op:'=', value:'0'}` or `{col:'candidates_count', op:'=', value:null}` (both match the declared type). ScopeTermSchema's numeric member is `value: z.number()`, and no other union member accepts col `candidates_count`, so the term fails, ScopeSchema fails, and AnalysisSchema fails — the batch is not partially triaged but rejected wholesale (the job's catch closes the day with an error and the orphans stay untriaged). The same mirror also leaves `col` and `op` as unconstrained strings, so `{col:'candidates_count', op:'contains', value:'x'}` has the same effect.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
raised.claim: recordEnrichFailure re-opens a row for triage (clearing review_class/review_note/reviewed_at) but leaves the v23 issue_number pointing at the old issue.
raised.why_it_breaks: When candidates_count crosses the 0↔>0 boundary the ON CONFLICT clause NULLs review_class/review_note/reviewed_at but never touches issue_number, so a row previously attached to #347 re-enters listUntriagedFailures still carrying issue_number = 347. The audit the v23 column was added for ("which rows went to this issue") then counts a row that is currently untriaged and may later be attached to a different issue; the stale link is only overwritten on the next setEnrichFailureReview call, and a row that is skipped forever keeps it.

raised.claim: A new issue whose legal scope is beer_ids-only can never accept another row, so recurrences of the same pattern are skipped forever.
raised.why_it_breaks: The prompt tells the model that `beer_ids` holds "the rows from today you are filing it for" and `where` is optional ("and/or"), and isLegalScope accepts a beer_ids-only scope. rowSatisfiesScope then returns true only for rows inside that fixed list. So an issue created with `{beer_ids:[...today...], where:[]}` is closed to every future row: tomorrow's recurrence of the same pattern hits guard 2, is counted as scope_violation, keeps review_class NULL, and recirculates in the batch indefinitely — exactly the stalled-backlog signal guardHits was added to surface.

raised.claim: guardHits.scope_violation conflates "issue has no block" with "row contradicts the scope", so the log cannot distinguish a missing ops backfill from a model misrouting.
raised.why_it_breaks: The PR states the one-time backfill of the 15 open orphan-triage issues is an ops step for after merge+deploy, and that until then every issue is unscoped and accepts nothing. In that window every single refusal takes the `target.scope === null` branch, so the `verdict shortfall` line reports scope_violation: N where N is fully explained by an unperformed ops step rather than by the model misrouting rows — the one-line visibility guardHits exists to provide is lost precisely when it is first needed.

raised.claim: The absence gate accepts a probe as proof when EITHER field is empty, so a name probe that returned hits is ignored whenever the brewery probe came back empty.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a row whose probe is `{brewery: '', name: 'Mad Elf, MadTree'}`, `proved` is true on the brewery term alone, so the not_on_untappd verdict survives and the row is written as not_on_untappd. isWebFallbackBlocked and the enrichment-pool predicate then treat it as established absence and stop retrying it, even though Untappd returned hits for the name — the啤酒 is listed, just under another brewery. The comment directly above states that hits from other breweries must not read as absence, which argues for requiring both probe fields empty (or vetoing on a non-empty name) rather than OR-ing them.
